headline: Google limits free Gemini to Flash-Lite starting October 9
dek: Flash and Pro leave the free plan, and the $4.99 Plus tier loses Pro too, pushing top-model access up to paid tiers, according to The Verge and Hipertextual.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Free Gemini drops to one model
body: Google will restrict its free Gemini plan to the Flash-Lite model starting October 9. Free users can pick Flash-Lite, Flash or Pro today; after the cutoff only Flash-Lite remains (The Verge, Hipertextual).
Paying users are hit too. Google AI Plus subscribers, at $4.99 a month, keep Flash and Flash-Lite but lose Gemini Pro. Google says it will email them with the exact date (The Verge).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: Three models, now split by price
s3.body: The models differ mainly in capability, not in message quotas. Flash-Lite stays uncapped on the free tier (Hipertextual).

points.t: Tuned for faster, lighter answers. The only model left for free users (Hipertextual).
Balances speed with somewhat deeper reasoning. Kept by Plus subscribers at $4.99 a month (The Verge).
The most capable of the three, built for multi-step analysis. Reserved for Google AI Pro and Ultra (The Verge).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Pro access gets more expensive
body: Keeping Gemini Pro and Deep Think, a mode that makes the model run more reasoning steps before answering, now takes Google AI Pro at $19.99 a month or Ultra at $99.99 (The Verge, Hipertextual).
Those most affected relied on the free or Plus tier for Pro-level reasoning on complex tasks. For them, the cheapest path to Pro is a fourfold jump from the Plus price (The Verge, Hipertextual).

stat.cap: a month, the new entry price for Pro (The Verge)

items.t: Last day free users can switch between Flash-Lite, Flash and Pro inside the Gemini app (The Verge, Hipertextual).
The free tier drops Flash and Pro, leaving Flash-Lite with no message cap (The Verge, Hipertextual).
Google will tell Plus subscribers exactly when they lose Gemini Pro access (The Verge).

caption.hook: Google will limit free Gemini to Flash-Lite from October 9, and the $4.99 Plus plan loses Gemini Pro as well.
body: Hipertextual calls it the biggest overhaul of Gemini since Google added a model picker to the app. Google had already introduced a dual rate limit, one cap resetting every 5 hours and another building over the week, the same structure Anthropic uses for Claude, and applied a similar restriction to NotebookLM.

The Pro and Ultra plans also differ on usage limits per model, cloud storage and bundled Google services (Hipertextual). Google keeps low, medium and high effort settings for each model; The Verge says high-effort Deep Think burns through limits faster.
